mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep edging up from their recent lows, weekday foot traffic will recover and pull RETAIL_REC modestly higher over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting proxies stall or reverse while retail stays flat or falls.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean within 4 weeks despite a continued upward move in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS above zero after a negative week signals improving discretionary outing intensity, which spills over into adjacent retail trips and lifts RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The effect breaks if PARKS stays negative or retail remains unchanged after the rebound.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below 0 to above 0 week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the next 14 days after PARKS moves from a negative weekly mean to a positive weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT stays depressed, people substitute toward local shopping and convenience retail rather than destination trips, which keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if residential intensity falls back or transit rebounds without a retail decline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and TRANSIT remains below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A broad late-summer uplift in PARKS together with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates more local errand-and-leisure activity, which should support RETAIL_REC over the next week. The signal is weak if PARKS does not stay above its recent average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher in the next weekly mean than in the current week despite PARKS staying above its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES falls more than five points in a week, the commuting channel weakens fast and retail visitation drops within two weeks. This mechanism fails when workplace mobility is stable or rising and RETAIL_REC still declines.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean within 14 days after a weekly drop in WORKPLACES greater than 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is a leading indicator of more in-person daytime circulation, and that should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if both commuting series rise but retail does not follow.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite concurrent increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, errands become more locally clustered and a fraction of those trips spill into nearby retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The effect fails if grocery access improves but retail traffic does not respond.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM stays above its prior-week level and RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: During a reopening regime, a rebound in TRANSIT from a depressed level should precede higher retail-and-recreation mobility because more riders generate more incidental shopping trips. The signal fails outside reopening conditions or if transit recovers without a retail increase.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two consecutive weeks after being below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days after TRANSIT rises for two straight weeks from below -25.
